items.corrected_text: The Métropole Aix-Marseille-Provence announced on 6 December 2023 a temporary offer of two free hours (between 10am and 7pm) in several metropolitan car parks, including La Ciotat's Vieux-Port and Centre Verdun, on the weekends of 9-10, 16-17 and 23-24 December 2023, to encourage Christmas shopping in town centres. The article describes it as temporary free parking.

All match. The article is from 2020 and says the free terms last only until the renovation ends; draft correctly notes current terms unchecked. corrected_summary: According to the La Ciotat tourist office, which is a secondary source for municipal rules, on-street parking is split into two paid zones. Zone 1 (centre-town streets and the La Tasse, Pétanque, Escalet and Sandral car parks) is listed as paid all year, 8am-8pm, with two free hours once a day. Zone 2 (the Mugel and Figuerolles car parks and streets near the beaches) is listed as paid only from 1 May to 30 September, 9am-8pm, with one free hour once a day. Both zones show the same rates of 3.80 EUR for the first hour and 38 EUR for ten hours, and a 38 EUR post-parking charge. The tourist office lists 15 car parks; the Port de Plaisance (255 spaces) is listed as paid from May to September and free from October to April, and two car parks are named as Indigo's (Vieux Port and Centre). In December 2023 the Métropole announced a temporary two-free-hours offer in the Vieux-Port and Centre Verdun car parks on three weekends. A 249-space car park opened at La Ciotat-Ceyreste station on 9 November 2020, free for up to seven days at that time and managed by RTM; current terms were not checked. The Calanques National Park strongly advises against driving into the town centre because of heavy visitor numbers and suggests car parks such as Mugel, which it says are not always supervised. The tourist office also maps 18 public charging locations. The city's own site could not be read, and the Métropole concession reports were not reached, so operator, capacity and utilisation figures are thin.
